title: Meet wreck-it
screen: README opening, followed by the running Gadgetly app
narration: Meet wreck it. It turns your coding agent into a QA team for your local web app.

title: Start locally
screen: Show the skills installation command and browser setup command. Cut to the app already running.
narration: Start your app locally, install the skills, and set up the browser tools. Your agent uses them to explore the app and record what breaks.

title: Choose a flow
screen: Real agent session: /wreck focus checkout. Briefly show its stated scope. Label any cut: time compressed.
narration: Ask it to test your app, or focus on one flow, like checkout. The agent walks through the flow, checks edge cases, and reproduces the problems it finds.

title: See the failure
screen: Gadgetly cart: change quantity from 1 to 3, blur the field, then click Checkout. Hold on the incorrect total.
narration: Here is a seeded demo bug. Three pairs of earbuds should total two hundred thirty-nine dollars and ninety-seven cents. Checkout displays just seventy-nine ninety-nine.

title: Get the evidence
screen: Open the finding, its cart and checkout screenshots, then lib/cart.ts:19. Highlight item.price.
narration: The finding includes reproduction steps, relevant screenshots, and the source location. Here, the subtotal adds each unit price once, ignoring the quantity.

title: Review and verify
screen: Show the HTML report, generated Playwright assertion, verified failing result, one-line correction, and passing result.
narration: Open the report and review the generated Playwright test. This check fails on the buggy copy, then passes after the subtotal calculation is corrected.

title: Try wreck-it
screen: End card: Wreck your app before your users do. github.com/miyannishar/wreck-it
narration: Try wreck it on your next local build. Wreck your app before your users do.
